knowledge:
- key_parameters: pct=Percentage of lowest variance genes to filter out in filter_low_var ;; type=Statistical measure to use for filtering in filter_low_var (e.g., "median" or "mean") ;; cor_func=Correlation method to use in build_net (defaults to "spearman") ;; n_threads=Number of threads to use for parallel processing in build_net ;; merge_threshold=Threshold for merging similar modules in detect_modules ;; keep_matrices=Saves correlation and adjacency matrices in build_net (set to "both" or TRUE) for downstream condition comparison ;; pvalue_th=Significance threshold for permutation tests in compare_conditions
- alternatives: WGCNA=GWENA wraps and simplifies several WGCNA functions (like pickSoftThreshold and adjacency) to reduce redundant correlation calculations and natively support Spearman correlation ;; NetRep=Used internally by compare_conditions for permutation testing of module preservation ;; g:Profiler (GOSt)=Used internally by bio_enrich for functional enrichment analysis ;; collapseRows (WGCNA)=Recommended for collapsing microarray probes to the gene level before running GWENA
- when_to_use: Use when you have normalized transcriptomics data (RNA-seq or microarray) and want to identify modules of co-expressed genes, perform functional enrichment, associate modules with clinical/phenotypic traits, identify hub genes, or compare co-expression networks across different experimental conditions.
- pitfalls: Do not use differentially expressed (DE) genes as a filter before network building, as unsupervised clustering relies on the scale-free property which DE filtering breaks ;; Ensure the input expression matrix has no missing (NA) values, as GWENA requires complete datasets ;; Plotting networks larger than 100 genes is highly resource-intensive; use upper_weight_th to filter out weak edges before plotting ;; High power fitting values can indicate strict thresholds, small sample sizes, or filtering that broke scale-free topology; low power fitting values can indicate strong batch effects or data heterogeneity.

workflows.name: single_condition_coexpression
workflows.intent: Perform gene co-expression network analysis, module detection, biological enrichment, phenotypic association, and visualization for a single experimental condition.
input: kuehne_expr (normalized expression matrix with genes as columns and samples as rows)
kuehne_traits (metadata/phenotype table with samples as rows)
workflows.stages: 1. Check expression data validity using is_data_expr ;; 2. Filter low variation genes using filter_low_var ;; 3. Build co-expression network using build_net ;; 4. Detect and merge modules using detect_modules ;; 5. Plot module merging using plot_modules_merge ;; 6. Perform functional enrichment using bio_enrich and plot with plot_enrichment ;; 7. Associate modules with phenotypes using associate_phenotype and plot with plot_modules_phenotype ;; 8. Build graph and sub-clusters using build_graph_from_sq_mat and get_sub_clusters ;; 9. Plot modules and sub-clusters using plot_module.
workflows.code:
is_data_expr(kuehne_expr)
kuehne_expr_filtered <- filter_low_var(kuehne_expr, pct = 0.7, type = "median")
kuehne_expr_filtered <- kuehne_expr_filtered[, 1:1000]
net <- build_net(kuehne_expr_filtered, cor_func = "spearman", n_threads = threads_to_use)
modules <- detect_modules(kuehne_expr_filtered, net$network, detailled_result = TRUE, merge_threshold = 0.25)
layout_mod_merge <- plot_modules_merge(modules_premerge = modules$modules_premerge, modules_merged = modules$modules)
enrichment <- bio_enrich(modules$modules)
plot_enrichment(enrichment)
phenotype_association <- associate_phenotype(modules$modules_eigengenes, kuehne_traits %>% dplyr::select(Condition, Age, Slide))
plot_modules_phenotype(phenotype_association)
module_example <- modules$modules$`2`
graph <- build_graph_from_sq_mat(net$network[module_example, module_example])
layout_mod_2 <- plot_module(graph, upper_weight_th = 0.999995, vertex.label.cex = 0, node_scaling_max = 7, legend_cex = 1)
net_mod_2 <- net$network[modules$modules$`2`, modules$modules$`2`] 
sub_clusters <- get_sub_clusters(net_mod_2)
layout_mod_2_sub_clust <- plot_module(graph, upper_weight_th = 0.999995, groups = sub_clusters, vertex.label.cex = 0, node_scaling_max = 7, legend_cex = 1)

workflows.name: multi_condition_comparison
workflows.intent: Compare gene co-expression networks and module preservation between different experimental conditions.
input: kuehne_expr (normalized expression matrix with genes as columns and samples as rows)
kuehne_traits (metadata/phenotype table with samples as rows)
workflows.stages: 1. Split expression data by condition ;; 2. Build networks for each condition using build_net with keep_matrices = "both" ;; 3. Detect modules for each condition using detect_modules ;; 4. Compare conditions using compare_conditions ;; 5. Plot comparison statistics using plot_comparison_stats.
workflows.code:
samples_by_cond <- lapply(kuehne_traits$Condition %>% unique, function(cond){
  df <- kuehne_traits %>% 
    dplyr::filter(Condition == cond) %>%
    dplyr::select(Slide, Exp)
  apply(df, 1, paste, collapse = "_")
}) %>% setNames(kuehne_traits$Condition %>% unique)

expr_by_cond <- lapply(samples_by_cond %>% names, function(cond){
  samples <- samples_by_cond[[cond]]
  kuehne_expr_filtered[which(rownames(kuehne_expr_filtered) %in% samples),]
}) %>% setNames(samples_by_cond %>% names)

net_by_cond <- lapply(expr_by_cond, build_net, cor_func = "spearman", 
                      n_threads = threads_to_use, keep_matrices = "both")

mod_by_cond <- mapply(detect_modules, expr_by_cond, 
                      lapply(net_by_cond, `[[`, "network"), 
                      MoreArgs = list(detailled_result = TRUE), 
                      SIMPLIFY = FALSE)

comparison <- compare_conditions(expr_by_cond, 
                                 lapply(net_by_cond, `[[`, "adja_mat"), 
                                 lapply(net_by_cond, `[[`, "cor_mat"),  
                                 lapply(mod_by_cond, `
[[`, "modules"), 
                                 pvalue_th = 0.05)

plot_comparison_stats(comparison$result$young$old$p.values)
